decisions.reason: A piqué upholstery fabric close to the core offer, with its own page, costs little to carry, and interior collections usually run several years, so the option stays open.
The bouclé-effect sheer had only a brief mention and its value is still unproven, but carrying a partner-produced collection fabric is cheap enough to wait one more season.
Flame-retardant contract fabrics depend on long hospitality specification cycles, so their value is still unfolding and they are worth holding at low cost.
The double-face wool blend supports the move toward renewable materials and has low carrying costs, so it is kept even though evidence of its demand is still limited.
The wool bouclé leno fits the sustainability direction but overlaps with other sheers in a broad portfolio, so it is kept for now with a heightened risk of being pruned.
The braided-structure fabric was launched only in 2024 and has its own page, so its uncertainty is high and keeping the option open is clearly worthwhile.
